title: Infection of a central line or heart device

items: A device infection happens when germs infect a tube placed into a vein (central line) or a heart device such as a pacemaker or defibrillator.
The device may need to be removed to clear the infection.
Fever, and redness, warmth or pus at the site.
Infection in the blood (bacteraemia) that does not clear.
Blood cultures from the line and from a vein in the arm.
A tip culture if the line is removed.
An echocardiogram (heart ultrasound) if there is a risk of heart valve infection.
Antibiotics are started based on the cultures.
Removing the line or device is often needed. Your team will decide.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Keep the site clean and dry, and tell the nurse about any redness or discharge.
Repeat blood cultures are often needed after treatment starts.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Fever with chills, or low blood pressure
Redness or pus at the line or device site, with pain
